# Sirach Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** All wisdom begins and ends with the Lord — it belongs to him forever.

**2** Who can count the grains of sand, the drops of rain, the days of ages past?

**3** Who can measure the heights of heaven, the span of the earth, the depths below?

**4** Before anything else existed, wisdom was already there — understanding present from the very beginning.

**5** Wisdom flows from the word of God on high; her paths are his eternal commands.

**6** Who has ever been shown wisdom's deepest roots? Who has understood her hidden ways?

**7** Who has been taught the full scope of wisdom's knowledge? Who has grasped everything she has seen?

**8** One alone is truly wise — the awesome Lord, enthroned above all.

**9** He is the one who created wisdom, looked upon her, measured her, and poured her out over everything he made.

**10** He gives her freely to all who love him; she lives among all people by his gift.

**11** Reverence for the Lord brings honor and glory — it is cause for celebration, a crown of joy.

**12** Reverence for the Lord fills the heart with delight, bringing joy, gladness, and a long life.

**13** Those who fear the Lord will find everything going well in the end; on the day they die, they will be called blessed.

**14** To revere the Lord — that is where wisdom begins. She was woven into those who are faithful from their very birth.

**15** Among the human family she has built her home, laying an eternal foundation; among those who follow after, she will be trusted.

**16** To be saturated with the fear of the Lord — that is true wisdom; she fills those who hold her with the fruit of all she has to give.

**17** She fills their whole household with beautiful things, their storerooms overflowing with her abundance.

**18** The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord — from it bloom peace and the fullness of health.

**19** He poured down knowledge and sound judgment, and he raised high the reputation of all who hold fast to her.

**20** The fear of the Lord is wisdom's root; long life grows from her branches.

**21** Reverence for the Lord drives sin away; wherever it takes hold, it turns back God's anger.

**22** A hotheaded person has no case to make — his own temper will be his undoing.

**23** A patient person waits for the right moment, and when it comes, joy will burst out like dawn.

**24** He holds his tongue until the time is right, and eventually everyone will praise his wisdom.

**25** Wisdom's treasury is full of instructive sayings — but to those who hate God, even worship is repulsive.

**26** Do you want wisdom? Keep the commandments. The Lord will give her to you freely.

**27** The fear of the Lord is both wisdom and discipline; what pleases him is loyalty and a humble heart.

**28** Do not defy the fear of the Lord; do not come to him with a split mind.

**29** Don't play a role for others to see — watch what comes out of your mouth.

**30** Don't raise yourself up — you will only fall and shame yourself. The Lord will uncover what you have hidden and bring you down before the whole community, because you did not truly come to fear him, and your heart was soaked through with deceit.
